title: Energy Shock Puts Bank of England Under Pressure to Raise Rates
summary: The Bank of England is facing mounting pressure to raise interest rates on Thursday amid a global bond market rout fuelled by concerns over runaway government borrowing and sticky inflation. Investors told Threadneedle Street it was “essential” to rein in prices before the energy shock triggered by the Iran war spreads through the economy and that failing to do so would risk the Bank “losing credibility”. title: Russia Extends Diesel Export Ban Through October
summary: Russia will extend its ban on diesel exports for all fuel producers to October 31, Vedomosti reported Tuesday, citing delayed refinery maintenance and the need to rebuild fuel reserves before winter. The ban, expanded in July from traders and small refineries to cover all producers, had been due to expire September 30. Diesel on the St. Petersburg commodity exchange traded at 70,546 rubles a ton in early September, and retail prices reached 88.44 rubles a liter on September 7, up 18.4% since the start of the year. title: TTF Gas Hits $92.95 as Gulf Tensions Weigh on Energy Markets
summary: Europe’s benchmark natural gas prices held above the 80-euro mark early on Wednesday, staying close to 2022 highs, as low gas volumes in storage sites fuel concerns about winter supplies amid continued disruption and widening conflict in the Middle East. The front-month price at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF), the benchmark for Europe’s gas trading, rose by 0.3% to $$92.95 (80.545 euros) per megawatt-hour (MWh) as of 9:15 a.m. in Amsterdam on Wednesday. title: New Zealand Dollar steadies against US Dollar as markets await Fed decision
summary: NZD/USD trades around 0.5755 at the time of writing on Wednesday, virtually unchanged on the day after rebounding from an over two-month low at 0.5737.

title: Sweeping Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill Advances Toward House Vote
summary: The US House Rules Committee has advanced legislation imposing tougher sanctions on Russia and Iran, clearing a key procedural hurdle for a possible House vote later this week but exposing deep Democratic concerns over the measure's expansion of presidential tariff authority. The committee voted 7-3 late on September 14 to advance a rule setting up debate on the legislation. Debate on the rule is expected to begin around noon local time on September 15. title: WTI pulls back below $100 as Saudi Arabia steps up efforts to restore Oil flows
summary: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil falls on Wednesday as Saudi Arabia steps up efforts to restore flows through its East-West pipeline, which was damaged by a drone attack last week.

title: Leaked EU Draft Would Scrap Hydrogen Mandates for EU-Wide Target
summary: A leaked European Commission impact assessment working document for the upcoming Renewable Energy Directive, RED IV, signals a potentially significant shift in renewable fuels policy after 2030. The draft's "preferred pacage" would replace binding national renewable hydrogen mandates with a more flexible EU-wide target, while giving greater room to crop-based biofuels and favoring advanced biofuels made from European feedstocks. title: Equinor Targets 15 Million Tons of LNG as Qatar Exports Stay Blocked
summary: Equinor plans to expand its global LNG portfolio to between 10 million and 15 million tons a year in the early 2030s, targeting European and Asian buyers left short on supply by the Strait of Hormuz blockade, Reuters reported Wednesday. The company expects to announce a second Asian supply agreement this week, Equinor LNG vice president Ingvar Egeland said.
